marie: Quick sync — need final decision on model capability flags + discovery endpoint shape by EOW. BigRetail asked for per-tenant streaming flags + explicit function-call signatures. Scope suggestion: flags + compact discovery response. Any major objections?

devin: +1. Proposal: discovery endpoint returns a capability matrix per model/version. Minimal flags: supports_streaming, max_input_tokens, max_total_tokens, supports_tools, tools_list (ids), structured_output (bool), structured_schema_url (opt), embeddings_dim, rerank_supported. Example below.

devin: ```json
{
  "model_id": "redwood-2.1",
  "version": "2026-02-10",
  "supports_streaming": true,
  "max_input_tokens": 8192,
  "max_total_tokens": 16384,
  "supports_tools": "soft",
  "tools_list": ["search.v1", "calendar.v1"],
  "structured_output": true,
  "structured_schema_url": "https://schemas.redwood.ai/models/redwood-2.1/output-v1.json",
  "embeddings_dim": 1536,
  "rerank_supported": true,
  "preferred_precision": "int8",
  "quantized_variants": ["int8", "int4"]
}
```

samir: Suggest we make supports_tools tri-state: "none" | "soft" | "strict". "soft" = can call tools but schema enforcement is not enforced by runtime; "strict" = runtime validates function signature/schema. Also we should include an explicit field for function signatures OR a URL to the function spec. Nested schemas are heavier but helpful for integrators.

qing: Docs note — all schema URLs must be HTTPS and versioned. Add fields: schema_version and discovery_generated_at. Also we should add a tiny 'notes' field for caveats.

patrick: Sales asks: customers need token limits + fallback behavior documented. Add fallback_model and fallback_policy (values: "truncate" | "reject" | "route"). They also want a short cost-implication hint if precision or quantization is present.

marie: OK. Draft launch criteria: 1) discovery endpoint returns capabilities for all public models; 2) docs + example SDK parsing; 3) per-model e2e tests verifying streaming flag and token caps; 4) migration guide for private/dedicated. If we meet these, mark as GA.

devin: From engineering: runtime already exposes `can_stream` and per-model token caps. We can compile the discovery manifest nightly. For Dedicated/Private we need per-tenant overrides — propose an optional overrides_url that points to a tenant manifest; server will consult overrides first.

samir: Add quantization/precision fields (preferred_precision, quantized_variants) — customers use this to estimate cost and latency. Also call out whether KV-cache is supported for long-context workloads (kv_cache_supported: true/false).

qing: I'll draft docs once schema is frozen. Proposed schedule: schema freeze Thu, docs draft Fri, publish Mon. @devin can you add an SDK helper and a parsing test?

devin: Yep. I'll open the PR tomorrow with a small helper `Discovery.parseCapabilities()` and unit tests. Will include sample parsing of streaming + function flags.

marie: :thumbsup: Keep discovery response compact — avoid large tool lists in the root, prefer references/urls. Add 'examples' page showing how to merge tenant overrides. Review Thurs 11:00am. Thanks everyone!
